lessonTitle: Breast, Thyroid and Endocrine Surgery: Lumps and the Triple Assessment

blocks.text: A 38-year-old teacher is told by her hairdresser that there is a lump at the front of her neck that rises when she swallows. She feels well, has no tremor or weight loss, and her pulse is 72. Whether that lump is a harmless colloid nodule or a papillary carcinoma will be decided by a structured pathway of tests, not by how it feels.

blocks.markdown: A swelling in the breast or the neck is managed by combining independent lines of evidence, so that no single imperfect test decides the outcome. In the breast, this is the **triple assessment**; in the thyroid, an equivalent logic combines ultrasound risk stratification with cytology. Endocrine surgery then applies a second principle: operate when the hormonal disorder cannot be controlled medically, causes complications, or is likely to be malignant.

blocks.title: Triple assessment
blocks.text: Triple assessment is the combination of (1) clinical assessment, (2) imaging (ultrasound, with mammography in older women) and (3) needle biopsy, preferably image-guided core biopsy giving histology, for every symptomatic breast lump. Each is graded, and the combined result is judged for concordance: if all three agree, the diagnosis is secure; if they disagree, further tissue (repeat or excision biopsy) is needed.

blocks.caption: Components of triple assessment with UK-style grading
rows: History, examination of both breasts and axillae
Ultrasound for women under about 40; mammography plus ultrasound from about 40
U1 to U5 (ultrasound); M1 to M5 (mammography)
Core needle biopsy (histology); fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) when core is unsuitable
B1 (unsatisfactory) to B5 (malignant); C1 to C5 for cytology

blocks.title: Judging concordance in a breast lump
blocks.prompt: A 47-year-old woman has a firm, irregular 2 cm lump in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast and a mobile axillary node. Examination is graded P4. Mammography is M5 and ultrasound U5 (irregular hypoechoic mass with posterior shadowing). Ultrasound-guided core biopsy shows B5b (invasive carcinoma). What conclusion do you draw?

steps.text: Clinical grade P4 indicates a lump suspicious of malignancy.
Mammography M5 and ultrasound U5 are both graded malignant, so imaging agrees with the clinical suspicion.
Core biopsy B5b gives histological proof of invasive cancer, and so all three components point to the same diagnosis.
Therefore the triple assessment is concordant malignant, and the case goes to the breast multidisciplinary team for staging and treatment planning.

blocks.answer: Concordant malignant triple assessment: invasive breast cancer, proceed to MDT discussion with staging and treatment planning.

blocks.markdown: **The thyroid nodule.** Palpable nodules are common and most are benign. First check thyroid function (TSH, then free T4 if abnormal). Perform ultrasound to describe the nodule using a scoring system such as the British Thyroid Association U1 to U5 scale. A suppressed TSH suggests a hyperfunctioning (toxic) nodule, which is almost never malignant and is characterised by isotope scintigraphy rather than needle biopsy. Suspicious sonographic features (microcalcifications, hypoechoic solid nodule, irregular or ill-defined margins, taller-than-wide shape, abnormal cervical nodes) prompt ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration cytology.

blocks.caption: Thyroid ultrasound and cytology categories (BTA)
rows: No FNAC needed in most cases
Reassure or repeat ultrasound as indicated
Atypia or follicular lesion; cannot exclude follicular carcinoma

blocks.title: Why follicular lesions go to surgery
blocks.text: Cytology looks at single cells. Distinguishing follicular adenoma from follicular carcinoma requires histology showing invasion of the capsule or blood vessels, so a follicular lesion (Thy3f) often needs diagnostic hemithyroidectomy.

blocks.markdown: **Surgery for hyperthyroidism.** Most Graves' disease and toxic nodular disease are first treated with antithyroid drugs (carbimazole) or radioiodine. Thyroidectomy is indicated for a large goitre with compressive symptoms (dysphagia, stridor), suspicion or proof of malignancy, relapse after drug treatment, failure or intolerance of drugs and radioiodine, moderate to severe active eye disease, or patient choice. The patient is made biochemically euthyroid first (antithyroid drugs, a beta-blocker for symptoms, and sometimes iodine solution before surgery for Graves' disease). **Primary hyperparathyroidism** (usually a single adenoma) is treated by parathyroidectomy when there are symptoms or complications, namely renal stones, osteoporosis or fragility fracture, reduced renal function, or marked hypercalcaemia (many guidelines use an adjusted calcium of about 2.85 mmol/L or higher), and in younger patients.

blocks.caption: A commonly used correction for albumin binding. Formulae and reference ranges vary by laboratory.

blocks.title: Adjusting calcium before deciding on parathyroidectomy
blocks.prompt: A woman with kidney stones has measured calcium 2.62 mmol/L and albumin 30 g/L. Using the formula above, what is the adjusted calcium and does it change the interpretation?

steps.text: Albumin is below 40 g/L, so measured calcium underestimates the active fraction.
Compare with the laboratory reference range, commonly about 2.20 to 2.60 mmol/L: 2.82 is clearly raised.

blocks.answer: Adjusted calcium 2.82 mmol/L: hypercalcaemia that the raw value understated. With stones it supports a diagnosis of primary hyperparathyroidism and surgical referral.

blocks.title: After thyroid or parathyroid surgery
blocks.text: Neck haematoma can compress the airway and needs immediate wound opening and senior help. Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury causes hoarseness; hypocalcaemia from parathyroid injury or hungry bone presents with perioral tingling and carpopedal spasm and is checked with serial calcium measurements.

points: Triple assessment (clinical, imaging, core biopsy) is graded and judged for concordance; discordant results need more tissue.
Thyroid nodules: TSH, ultrasound risk grade, FNAC for suspicious or indeterminate nodules; follicular lesions may need diagnostic hemithyroidectomy.
Thyroidectomy for hyperthyroidism is indicated for compression, malignancy, drug or radioiodine failure, relapse, severe eye disease or patient choice.
Parathyroidectomy for primary hyperparathyroidism is indicated by symptoms, stones, bone or renal complications or marked hypercalcaemia.

questions.stem: Which set correctly lists the three components of triple assessment of a symptomatic breast lump?

options.text: Clinical examination, imaging, and needle biopsy
History, blood tumour markers, and CT

questions.correctOptionText: Clinical examination, imaging, and needle biopsy

distractorRationale.b: Tumour markers and CT are not part of triple assessment.
distractorRationale.c: MRI and open excision are not routine components.
distractorRationale.d: These are all imaging; there is no clinical or pathological component.

questions.explanation: Triple assessment uses three independent forms of evidence: clinical, imaging and tissue. Agreement among them gives a very low false-negative rate.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman has a smooth, mobile 1.5 cm breast lump. Which imaging is generally first-line?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: dense breast tissue in younger women favours ultrasound.
distractorRationale.b: Mammography is less sensitive in dense young breasts and exposes to radiation.
distractorRationale.c: Bone scan is a staging test.
distractorRationale.d: CT chest is not used to assess a breast lump.

questions.explanation: In women under about 40 the breast is dense, so ultrasound distinguishes cystic from solid lesions better than mammography. Mammography is added from about 40 years.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman has a hard fixed breast lump (P5) and ultrasound U5, but core biopsy reports B2 (benign). What is the appropriate next step?

options.text: Treat the result as discordant and obtain further tissue, by repeat core biopsy or excision biopsy
Reassure and discharge because the biopsy is benign

questions.correctOptionText: Treat the result as discordant and obtain further tissue, by repeat core biopsy or excision biopsy

distractorRationale.a: Correct: two suspicious components and one benign result are discordant and unreliable.
distractorRationale.b: Missing a cancer through a sampling error is the exact risk concordance avoids.
distractorRationale.d: Treatment cannot start without a tissue diagnosis.

questions.explanation: A benign biopsy cannot override clinically and radiologically malignant findings because the needle may have missed the tumour. Discordant triple assessment demands repeat sampling or excision before the lump is declared benign.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man has a solitary 2 cm thyroid nodule found on neck ultrasound for another reason. His TSH is normal. Ultrasound shows a hypoechoic solid nodule with microcalcifications. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Start levothyroxine to shrink the nodule

distractorRationale.a: Correct: suspicious sonographic features warrant cytology.
distractorRationale.b: Radioiodine is for hyperthyroidism or after cancer surgery.
distractorRationale.d: Thyroxine suppression does not treat suspicious nodules.

questions.explanation: Microcalcifications and a hypoechoic solid pattern are suspicious sonographic features, so cytology is required. Normal TSH makes a hyperfunctioning nodule unlikely.

questions.stem: FNAC of a 3 cm thyroid nodule reports a follicular lesion (Thy3f). Why is diagnostic hemithyroidectomy often advised?

options.text: Cytology cannot distinguish follicular adenoma from carcinoma; invasion is shown only on histology
Cytology of follicular lesions is always diagnostic of adenoma
Hemithyroidectomy is needed to treat hyperthyroidism

questions.correctOptionText: Cytology cannot distinguish follicular adenoma from carcinoma; invasion is shown only on histology

distractorRationale.a: Correct: capsular or vascular invasion is a histological diagnosis.
distractorRationale.b: Most follicular lesions are benign adenomas.
distractorRationale.d: The indication is diagnostic uncertainty, not hyperthyroidism.

questions.explanation: Follicular carcinoma is defined by invasion of capsule or vessels, which needs the whole lesion on histology. Surgery therefore both diagnoses and, if benign, treats.

questions.stem: Which patient has the clearest indication for parathyroidectomy?

options.text: A woman with biochemically confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism and recurrent renal stones
A patient with secondary hyperparathyroidism from vitamin D deficiency
A patient with normal calcium and normal PTH
A patient with hypocalcaemia and low PTH

questions.correctOptionText: A woman with biochemically confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism and recurrent renal stones

distractorRationale.a: Correct: primary disease with a complication (stones) is an accepted indication.
distractorRationale.b: Secondary disease responds to correcting the cause.
distractorRationale.d: This is hypoparathyroidism, not a surgical problem.

questions.explanation: Parathyroidectomy cures primary hyperparathyroidism and is indicated when symptoms or complications such as stones, bone disease or renal impairment are present. Secondary hyperparathyroidism is treated medically by addressing the underlying cause.

questions.stem: A man with a fragility fracture has measured calcium 2.71 mmol/L and albumin 28 g/L. Using adjusted Ca = measured Ca + 0.02 x (40 - albumin), calculate the adjusted calcium in mmol/L.
questions.explanation: The albumin deficit is 40 - 28 = 12 g/L, which adds 0.02 x 12 = 0.24 mmol/L, giving 2.71 + 0.24 = 2.95 mmol/L. This exceeds the roughly 2.85 mmol/L level at which many guidelines recommend surgery in primary hyperparathyroidism.

questions.stem: A patient with Graves' disease should be rendered biochemically euthyroid before elective thyroidectomy.
questions.explanation: Operating on a thyrotoxic patient risks a thyroid storm with arrhythmia and haemodynamic collapse. Antithyroid drugs, a beta-blocker and sometimes iodine are used to control thyroid hormone excess beforehand.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with a 2 cm firm thyroid nodule and normal thyroid function. Describe how you would evaluate the nodule and what the results would mean.
markingGuide: History and examination: rapid growth, hoarseness, family history, radiation, cervical nodes
TSH and free T4; suppressed TSH suggests toxic nodule needing scintigraphy
Ultrasound with risk stratification (U1 to U5) and suspicious features: microcalcification, hypoechoic, irregular margins, taller-than-wide, abnormal nodes
Ultrasound-guided FNAC for indeterminate or suspicious nodules, reported as Thy1 to Thy5
Thy3f follicular lesion: diagnostic hemithyroidectomy; Thy4 or Thy5: MDT and surgery
Thy2 benign: reassurance and follow-up as indicated
questions.explanation: Evaluation combines function tests, ultrasound risk grade and cytology. Results classify the nodule as benign, indeterminate or malignant and direct follow-up or surgery.

questions.stem: Outline the indications for surgery in hyperthyroidism and in primary hyperparathyroidism, and name two early complications of neck endocrine surgery with their recognition.
markingGuide: Hyperthyroidism: compressive goitre, malignancy or suspicion, relapse after antithyroid drugs, intolerance or failure of drugs and radioiodine, severe eye disease, patient choice
Primary hyperparathyroidism: symptoms, stones, osteoporosis or fracture, renal impairment, marked hypercalcaemia (adjusted Ca around 2.85 mmol/L or higher), younger age
Neck haematoma causing airway compromise, needs urgent wound opening
Hypocalcaemia with perioral tingling or carpopedal spasm, check calcium
Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury causes hoarseness
questions.explanation: Surgery is reserved for patients who cannot be controlled medically or who have complications or suspected cancer. Early complications relate to the neck anatomy: bleeding, nerve injury and parathyroid dysfunction.
